modificationDescription: Ultimate-owned, scoped-down reimplementation of PrimeReact's ComponentBase. Verified source: cx() resolves css.classes[key](params) (ComponentBase.js lines ~511-513). Ultimate decision: excludes the full pt/ptm/ptmo passthrough system (~150 lines of nested-key resolution in the verified source) entirely, per spec §7's Option B posture — no demonstrated Ultimate consumer need, same YAGNI justification as Angular's ADR-018. Amended in Task 14 (UButton): ClassValue's Record<string, boolean> widened to Record<string, boolean | undefined>, since a boolean? prop passed straight into a boolean-modifier class-name record position naturally types as boolean | undefined -- resolveClassValue()'s classNames() call already treats undefined and false identically at runtime, so this is a pure type-widening fix with no behavior change, made once here so every future component's style module (checkbox/dialog/menu, Tasks 16-18) doesn't have to locally re-patch around the same gap.

Verified upstream behavior: bind/unbind pair attaching/detaching a listener on a resolved target (supports 'window'/'document' string targets and function-resolved targets), gated by a `when` flag. Critical bug fix, round 2 (found by re-review of the Task 18/UMenu round-1 fix, commit b8a32d7 — round 1, commit ca83432, was necessary but insufficient): boundRef was a plain boolean recording only whether something was bound, never which function object addEventListener actually received. unbind()'s removeEventListener(type, listener) used whatever `listener` closure was in scope at unbind time, which only matches the bind-time function if the caller's listener prop has a stable identity across every render between bind and unbind — a useCallback wrapper at the call site (round 1's fix) only holds that stability when ITS OWN deps are stable, and UMenu's `hide` callback is useCallback(..., [visible]), where `visible` is exactly the value that flips between the bind-time render and the unbind-time render (from useMotion's onAfterLeave) by design. No amount of useCallback wrapping at any call site could fix this — it was structural to this hook. Empirically reproduced (reviewer's own document.addEventListener/removeEventListener instrumentation) that the round-1-only fix still leaked: 1 live listener after dismissal (should be 0), 1 permanently after unmount-while-visible, and 1→2→3 accumulating across 3 open/close cycles. Fixed at the root: stores the exact bound function in a ref (boundListenerRef, replacing the boolean boundRef) inside bind(), and unbind() removes boundListenerRef.current rather than a re-derived `listener` value — correct regardless of the current-render listener identity. Also fixes the resize-listener path (routes through this same hook, independently verified) and UMenu's useUnmountEffect (empty deps, closes over the first render's unbindOverlay closure) automatically, since unbind() no longer depends on which render's closure calls it. Empirically re-verified post-fix using the reviewer's own methodology: 0 live listeners after dismissal, 0 after unmount-while-visible, 0→0→0 across 3 cycles (no accumulation).

Verified upstream behavior: a window-resize-specific specialization of the event-listener bind/unbind pattern. Implemented here as a thin wrapper over useEventListener rather than a duplicate implementation.

Verified upstream behavior (Portal.js): DomHandler.isClient()-guarded mount state, ReactDOM.createPortal to a resolved appendTo target defaulting to document.body, appendTo==='self' renders inline instead of portaling. Reimplemented as isClient()-equivalent check + useMountEffect, not ported line-for-line. Ultimate decision: excludes PrimeReactContext-based appendTo default and onMounted/onUnmounted callback props present in the verified source — no demonstrated Ultimate consumer need, per YAGNI.

Verified upstream behavior: composite outside-click + resize (+ orientationchange + overlay-scroll, not included here) dismissal listener. Ultimate decision: scoped to outside-click + resize only, matching the Phase 3 proof set's actual UMenu popup-mode usage — orientationchange/scroll composition deferred until a real consumer needs it, per YAGNI. Behavioral deviation from verified upstream: the outside-click handler in Portal.js's PrimeReact original always invokes `listener` with a computed `valid` flag, leaving validity checks to the caller; this Ultimate implementation instead gates the call internally and only invokes `listener` when the click is genuinely outside both target and overlay, matching this task's own test contract (a click on the target must not invoke the listener at all, not invoke it with valid:false). Critical bug fix (found in Task 18/UMenu review, commit ca83432): the document-click and window-resize listeners passed internally to useEventListener/useResizeListener were fresh inline arrow functions constructed on every render of this hook. useEventListener's own bind/unbind are useCallback-memoized keyed on that listener reference, so a new reference every render silently defeated the memoization — addEventListener and the later removeEventListener ended up targeting different function objects, and removeEventListener no-ops on a mismatched reference, so the document click listener outlived every unbind/unmount call (first exposed by UMenu, this hook's first and only real consumer at the time; reproduced impact: outside-click dismissal of a popup UMenu left a live document listener that re-fired hide()/onHide for every subsequent unrelated click, surviving even component unmount). Fixed by wrapping both listeners in useCallback with correct deps ([isOutsideClicked, listener] and [listener] respectively), so useEventListener's bind/unbind memoization actually holds across renders. This bug was in this hook's own implementation from Task 5, not introduced or caused by any Task 18 code; the identical inline-listener pattern also existed at UMenu's own call site into this hook and was fixed there too (see the Menu.js entry in react.json).

Ultimate-authored test, not derived from upstream. Extended in the Task 18/UMenu review fix, round 1 (commit ca83432) with a regression test that binds from one render and unbinds from a later render's closure — the exact timing that exposed the stale-listener-reference bug (see the use-overlay-listener.ts entry above); RED-verified against the pre-fix code (listener fired twice instead of once) before the fix, GREEN after. Round 1's test was itself self-defeating, found in round 2's re-review (commit b8a32d7): it held the `listener` prop's identity constant across its rerender() call, so even round 1's insufficient useCallback-only fix would pass it — the test never actually exercised a changed listener identity, the real failure mode. Rewritten to rerender() with a genuinely different listener function and assert the ORIGINAL listener (the one actually bound) stops firing after unbind(); a parallel resize-listener test was added (verified independently affected by the same root cause). Both RED-verified against round 1's still-buggy use-event-listener.ts (click test: listener fired twice; resize test: fired once when it should never fire) before round 2's fix, GREEN after.

Verified upstream behavior: a single shared document keydown listener gated by a two-level [primaryPriority, secondaryPriority] tuple map, only the highest tuple's callback fires, listener attaches/detaches based on whether any registration exists. Independently authored per spec §11 — this is more correct than Angular's existing UDialog Escape handling (ADR-020's documented gap: no multi-dialog stacking), and this reimplementation is what closes that gap for React.

Verified upstream mechanism: hidden sentinel-span pair bracketing children, onFocus handlers on each sentinel redirect real DOM focus back into the trapped region via getFirstFocusableElement/getLastFocusableElement lookups. Reuses @ultimate/uix-utils's already-built getFirstFocusableElement/getLastFocusableElement (already consumed today by Angular's UFocusTrap/UAutoFocus) rather than reimplementing focusable-element lookup. Materially different mechanism than Angular's UFocusTrap (keydown Tab/Shift+Tab interception) — intentional, per spec §14. Simplified relative to verified source: does not distinguish forward-vs-backward cycling direction via relatedTarget, since the Phase 3 proof set's only consumer (UDialog) is a single-level, non-nested trap. No test file exists for FocusTrap in PrimeReact 10.9.9 (verified absent) — this test suite is entirely Ultimate-authored.

Ultimate-authored test — no upstream test file exists to adapt from. One assertion deviates from the plan's literal brief: the 'does not auto-focus when disabled' test originally compared document.activeElement?.textContent to "Inside", which cannot distinguish "the button is focused" from "nothing is focused (activeElement is <body>)" in jsdom, since the button's text is the only text content in the document either way and body.textContent trivially equals "Inside" in both cases. Verified via isolated debug runs that the implementation's disabled-mount behavior is correct (activeElement stays <body>, matching the non-disabled/autoFocus=false-default case, versus the button actually receiving focus when autoFocus is explicitly true). Fixed the assertion to compare element identity (document.activeElement is the body, and is not the button element) instead of textContent, preserving the test's intent while making it capable of actually catching a regression.

Verified upstream behavior: document.primeDialogParams tracks {id, hasBlockScroll} per mounted-and-visible Dialog, updateScrollBlocker() checks .some(i => i.hasBlockScroll) across all instances. Ultimate decision (intentional deviation, spec §16): replaced the global document-property mutation with a private module-scoped Set<string> registry — coalesces the same way (scroll blocked while >=1 dialog registered), calls @ultimate/uix-utils/dom's already-built blockBodyScroll/unblockBodyScroll only at the 0->1/1->0 boundary transitions, matching verified behavior without exposing a public global.

Ultimate-authored test, including explicit multi-dialog 0->1/1->0 transition regression coverage per spec §23 — no upstream test file exists to adapt from (Dialog.js has zero PrimeReact-authored tests, verified during the gate). One deviation from the plan's literal brief: added an afterEach that drains the registry (calls unregister for every id used across this file's tests) via the hook's own public API. Root cause: useScrollLock's blockingIds Set is an intentionally private, module-scoped singleton (not exported, not a document property, by design) that outlives any single renderHook call — without explicit cleanup, an id registered in one test (e.g. 'registering the first dialog blocks body scroll' leaves 'dialog-1' registered) leaked into the next test's initial state, making a later register() see the registry as already non-empty and skip the block call, even though beforeEach reset document.body.className. This is a test-isolation gap, not a hook logic bug: in production, UDialog instances always call unregister on unmount, so the registry self-cleans; the test suite must do the same explicitly since nothing else resets the module singleton between test runs. Confirmed via isolated debug instrumentation before concluding this was a test bug rather than an implementation bug.

Verified upstream behavior: creates a real <style data-primereact-style-id> element, dedupes by name, appends to document.head, SSR-safe. Ultimate decision: does NOT port useStyle.js's implementation — instead subclasses the already-built, framework-neutral @ultimate/uix-styled StyleSheet (whose base createStyleElement is a documented no-op, confirmed by an existing uix-styled test), overriding createStyleElement to delegate to the already-built @ultimate/uix-utils/dom createStyleElement. This closes a real, previously-undocumented gap: Angular's ngCoreStyleSheet never overrides this hook either, so no <style> element is currently injected by Angular's style-registration path. Per spec §8's explicit decision, this task fixes it for React only; the Angular-side gap is recorded as a new Phase 2 follow-up (Task 20), not fixed here. Deviation from the plan's literal brief: the brief's sample code imports StyleSheet as a default export (`import StyleSheet, { type StyleMeta } from "@ultimate/uix-styled"`), but @ultimate/uix-styled's built package (packages/uix-styled/dist/index.mjs, generated from src/index.ts's `export { default as StyleSheet, ... } from "./stylesheet/index"`) only exposes StyleSheet as a named export from the package root — confirmed by inspecting the built dist output directly (a bare default import resolved to `undefined`, causing `class ReactStyleSheet extends StyleSheet` to throw 'Class extends value undefined is not a constructor'). This matches the existing precedent in packages/ng-core/src/basecomponent/style-sheet.ts, which already imports `{ StyleSheet } from "@ultimate/uix-styled"` the same way. Fixed to `import { StyleSheet, type StyleMeta } from "@ultimate/uix-styled"`; StyleMeta itself is genuinely a named type export in both source and dist, unaffected.

Same treatment as spinner-icon.tsx above: path data ported verbatim, passthrough spread excluded. Structural deviation from the Spinner template: the verified upstream <path> here carries fillRule="evenodd" and clipRule="evenodd" attributes (a compound-shape icon: outer window frame plus an inner arrow/corner glyph in one path), which Spinner's single simple path does not have. Ported both attributes verbatim onto the React <path> element (React accepts these as camelCase SVG props) rather than omitting them, since dropping them would change the rendered shape (evenodd fill-rule affects which sub-regions of a self-intersecting path are painted).
